IB IV, 53 (ח33). Letter previously thought to be from Abū Yaʿqūb Ibn al-Najera, somewhere in Spain, to Ḥalfon b. Netanel, likely in Lucena. Dating: likely August 1138 CE. 
Identifications and datings are based on comparison with T-S 12.285. [However, T-S AS 149.119 is a letter from Ibn al-Najera and does not resemble this one.] This letter recounts the writer's visit to a woman who owed him 10 mithqāls, but he found her sick. He now asks Ḥalfon to advance him a certain sum, probably the same 10 mithqāls, for the purpose of his travel to Almeria. Information from Goitein and Friedman, India Bo
Accounts in Arabic script, unclear if state or private or communal. May refer to a qinṭār of glass and the phrase "maʿa al-mawjūd fī l-ḥamām(?)." Needs examination. On recto there is piyyuṭ.

Minute fragment from a late legal deed regarding marriage (or perhaps inheritance?): או תפטר מ שרה הנז׳ בחיי ב[עלה] ... בעלה הנז׳ בחייה תהיה חזקת ה. Only the first name Sarah is available among the legal parties original mentioned in the document (with a clause regarding what should happen if her husband dies and leaves her a widow).
Probably a commercial letter or legal document. In Hebrew. Small fragment, with only a few words preserved. Dating: Perhaps 15th–17th century. Mentions white pepper (פלפל לבן).
Letter, mostly faded (the first few words of each line are effaced) written by Mevorakh b. Natan (Date: 1150–81). Might be a formulary.

Verso: Official letter/order from the office of one of the later Maimonidean Nagids, with motto/ʿalāma at the top. Similarly concerns the releasing a vow between Yiṣḥaq and Ṣedaqa b. ʿEli. May have been written in response to verso, though the names aren't the same. (Information in part from Goitein's index card.)

Letter fragment on parchment. Probably a letter of appeal for assistance, written in a flowery style in a mixture of Hebrew and Judaeo-Arabic. Most of the preserved text consists of blessings for the community to which the letter is addressed, potentially Latakia in Syria (לאתקיאיה in l. 7, an unusual spelling but the letters are clear). The letter originates in Spain or the Maghrib and dates to the period 1086–1147 CE, probably the earlier part of that range, based on the reference to the Almoravid invasions: "the Almoravids descended upon us and burned and plundered and killed. . . ." (l. 11
Minute fragment. Few words from the top of a legal deed.

Probably a business letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Late. Mentions transactions, numbers, and people such as Avraham and Shemuʾel. The currency is repeatedly referred to as "אשפרי", likely the Ottoman akçe (aka asper, aspros). However, line 10 might refer to gold fındıklı coinage, which would help to date this fragment as post-1725, but the spelling is unclear (?פנדוק.לי). It is uncommon for akçe and fındıklı to be referenced in the same geniza fragments. By the 1700s the akçe served more so as a unit of account rather than physical coinage. Requires further examination.

Draft of a letter written either by Avraham Maimonides or his son David I Maimonides (their hands are almost identical). The fact that the opening phrase (גרץ תסטירהא etc.) is identical to that of T-S 16.343 (PGPID 7489) may tilt the probability in favor of David being the writer. The letter is probably addressed to a physician known as al-Rashīd ("al-ḥaḍra... al-ḥakīmiyya al-rashīdiyya..."). It concerns al-Shaykh al-Thiqa Hiba, perhaps Hibat[allāh b. Abū] l-Faraj. The draft is repeated on verso. AA. ASE.

Medical prescription in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: Probably 12th or 13th century based on handwriting. Partial transcription on Goitein's index card. On recto there is a poem on the history of the Patriarchs in rhymed Judaeo-Arabic (Goitein wonders: "a haggada for women?")
Possibly a document (needs examination)

Letter from Yosef b. Farah from Alexandria to Abu Ya’aqov Ishaq, Fustat. Around 1057. The writer tries to get a copy of a teshuva by Hanan”el b. Hushi”el in the possession of Labrāṭ b. Moshe b. Sughmār from Mahdiyya. It is not clear what the content of the teshuva is and who received it. The letter was written shortly after the passing of Hananʾel. (Information from Gil, Kingdom, Vol. 3, #516) VMR
Formulary or draft of the opening of a petition to a vizier and qāḍī. Cuts off right after the "wa-yunhī."

Deed of sale of a property on recto, with multiple related addenda documents on verso. Dated 2 Muḥarram 777 AH on recto (1375 CE). In the introduction to her edition, Jane Hathaway notes: "In this badly torn sharīʿa court document, dated 2 Muḥarram 777 AH/3 June 1375 CE, an unnamed woman transfers one-quarter of a large house to her son Sharaf al-Dīn Mūsā. Much of the documentʾs recto comprises a description of the property and its boundaries. The house is located in Ḥārat Zuwayla, a neighbourhood in the northwest of the original Fatimid city of al-Qāhira, southwest of Bāb al-Futūḥ and northwe

Accounts probably. In Judaeo-Arabic on one side and two different documents in Arabic script on the other written at 180 degrees (part of the Arabic script reads like a letter). Mentions Ibn Wuhayb. (Information in part from CUDL)
Accounts with Coptic numerals. On margin formulae from a legal document. (Information from CUDL)

Possibly a fragment from a historical chronicle. In Judaeo-Arabic. On parchment. Refers to "the son of Khosrow the king of Persia" בן כסרי מלך אלפרס . . . . אלשמס ואלי לחאלה . . . מע דלאל . . . דלך מן אל . . . ועשר עשר . . .
A letter, probably business, with a list of some items(?) at the bottom. Damaged.
Receipt for the capitation tax of Khalaf b. Ghālib the Jew, a druggist (ʿaṭṭār) and something else (jabbān? jazzār?) in Fustat for the year 504 AH (or 540?).

Report (official state correspondence). 6 lines from the middle section are preserved. Refers to audiences with the caliph, the amīr Wajīh al-Dawla, and someone traveling from Ramla to Damascus via Banyas and (then?) to Sidon. Reused on recto for piyyuṭ.
Late accounts, it seems mainly or entirely in Ladino. Terms mentioned: מונידא ,דוקתי ,שולדי ,אשקודי. Merits examination.

Court record. In Judaeo-Arabic. In a Yemeni hand (Worman's handlist desribes it as "Modern Yemenite.") concerning a debt of 2.5 qirsh between Ṣaliḥ b. Mūsā ʿUmīsī and Ḥasan b. Sālim Mūsā Zanār. Several witnesses: Sālim Ḥadī (חדי), Ḥasan al-Dhīb (אלדיב, wolf), Yaḥyā Hārūn (ṣāḥib al-qumʿa(?)), Mūsā Nissīm, and Menaḥem (?). (Information in part from CUDL)
Minute fragment from the end of a legal deed. Very damaged. Only some signatures preserved: […] ha-Levi b. Avraham, Yehuda b. Moshe ha-Mumḥe. Reused for Hebrew literary text.AA
Small fragment from a legal deed, probably regarding dispute based on the reference to זקני יושר

Letter segment concerning some legal issues with the signature of Shemarya. The first concerns Nissim al-Iskandarani who has entered into a business partnership with an unnamed woman. Then mentions a request for something to be sent to Mūsā the ghulām of Ibn ʿEzra; an agent who should present something to the court; David; and an order for an item (likely a carpet) for the Bet Midrash measuring 12 by 3.5 cubits. Greetings are sent at the end to Yosef b. Salim. (Information in part from CUDL)

Recto: two documents. 

The first (bottom) is an order for delivery of dues to the office of land tax (dīwān al-kharāj) written by the accountant Abū Musabbiḥī Abū l-Qāsim al-Ḥasan b. al-Ḥusayn, in which it is stated that Abū l-Ḥasan Mājid b. Yaʿqūb shall deliver to the land-tax office the dues that he received from Wasly b. Maymūn and that went through the hands of Abū Qalā ʿAbd al-Raḥmān […], Zakariyā b. Mukhtār, ʿAlūn b. Ḥanūn (the clerk), Ṣayfī b. Rashīd and Qolte b. al-Sarrī (surveyors). Dated: 423 AH, which is 1031/32 CE. 

The second document (top, 90 degrees) is a receipt issued by
Letter, probably. In Judaeo-Arabic, elevated register. Small fragment only. Mentions the government. (Information in part from CUDL)

Business letter in Judaeo-Arabic. Dating: likely 12th or early 13th century. Concerning a trip of the addressee and a third person, and mentioning 80 dirhams in the possession of someone else and the arrival and news of yet another person. Mentions staying in al-Maḥalla Wednesday night; meeting with Makīn b. Mukhtār, who reported his intention to travel and that 80 jars of his wine had turned to vinegar; also mentions al-Shaykh al-Rashīd; and good quality wheat.
Letter from Farah b. Yusuf sending condolences for the death of a relative of the addressee and also discussing business. (Information from Gil)
